Scientific layout — full button inventory

Satisfies AC3

All 14 required functions are present: sin, cos, tan, asin (sin⁻¹), acos (cos⁻¹), atan (tan⁻¹), log, ln, exponent (xʸ), square (x²), square root (√), π, e, and factorial (n!). These render above the basic grid, which stays visible underneath.

Basic layout — full button inventory

Satisfies AC4

Only digits 0–9, decimal point, + − × ÷, "=", "C" (clear) and "CE" (clear entry) — no scientific function button is present or reachable while Basic is active.

Keyboard focus order

Satisfies AC5
  1. Tab from the dialog's close button reaches the layout toggle: Basic, then Scientific — each activates on Enter or Space.
  2. Continuing Tab in Scientific layout reaches every scientific key in reading order (sin → cos → tan → log → sin⁻¹ → … → e), then every basic key (CE → C → ÷ → 7 → … → "=").
  3. Continuing Tab in Basic layout skips straight from the toggle to the basic keys — the scientific keys are not focus stops at all, since the hidden attribute removes them from the page's focus order and the accessibility tree.
  4. Shift+Tab reverses the same order in both layouts.

Touch target sizing

Satisfies AC6
48 × 48px — scientific key
58 × 58px — basic key

Both comfortably clear the 44 × 44px minimum.

Assistive-tech announcement

Satisfies AC7
"Scientific layout active. 14 additional function buttons are now available: sine, cosine, tangent, inverse sine, inverse cosine, inverse tangent, log, ln, exponent, square, square root, pi, e, and factorial."
"Basic layout active. Only digits, decimal point, the four arithmetic operators, equals, and clear are shown."

A visually-hidden aria-live="polite" region speaks this every time the toggle is activated, independent of the visible button set changing.
